method: Real web research (same pass as zurkt-access-external-evidence-v4.json, 2026-09-13). Mixture probabilities below are informed by confirmed species/plantation-status evidence, not a point classification -- residual uncertainty is retained (e.g. a confirmed 'pine + eucalyptus' plantation still carries some probability mass on 'mixed_plantation' and 'unresolved' rather than 100% on one class) because none of these sources give exact species-area breakdowns.

cfrs.rationale: Confirmed 80% planted, pine (P. caribaea, P. oocarpa) + eucalyptus (E. grandis) -- FSC Forest Management certified. Species mix not given as an exact area split, so eucalyptus/pine/mixed retain comparable probability mass.
Confirmed hybrid eucalyptus clones (GC/GU) as the primary product line (utility poles, timber), pine present but secondary per Green Resources' own 2024 corporate profile.
Confirmed pine + eucalyptus plantation (New Forests Company), no area split by species found -- treated as roughly even mixed plantation.
Same New Forests Company plantation program as Namwasa, same species pattern, no area split by species found.

Nileply Ltd confirmed to have planted eucalyptus on ~1,500 ha of the 16,382 ha reserve (~9%) -- most of the CFR's area has NOT been confirmed as plantation, so natural/mixed and degraded-open still dominate the mixture.
Confirmed predominantly natural moist semi-deciduous tropical forest, zoned (strict nature reserve / buffer / production), not an enrolled timber plantation.

Confirmed natural/mixed forest (106 tree species documented), NFA direct management, no plantation evidence found -- weighted toward natural/degraded given noted weak enforcement and encroachment context.

Confirmed severe historical encroachment/clearing, >80% forest cover loss reported for the district, active degazettement directive -- weighted heavily toward degraded/open, not toward any plantation or intact natural class.
Confirmed ~70% cleared by encroachers per cited environmental reporting -- weighted toward degraded/open.
Academic literature explicitly describes this CFR as 'severely degraded' with active restoration/replanting -- weighted toward degraded/open with some replanting-derived plantation probability.
